source.kind: user-provided screenshots of the 143-page Hybrid Marketing deck
source.note: Screenshots include surrounding contiguous panels in addition to visible page counters. They reinforce selected visual claims; they are not a replacement for the full source. Duplicate screenshots are hash-deduplicated.

visual_findings.source_observation: The funnel deliberately routes through both L-step and email even though the list shrinks to about 65%, framing the loss as screening for better-fit customers rather than pure failure.
The material explicitly describes sunk-cost/self-justification effects and a paid closing session as mechanisms that can increase purchase inclination.
The material distinguishes coercion from nudging while preserving an apparent choice path.
visual_findings.attack_translation: A Human Gate cannot be treated as meaningful authorization merely because a click occurred; refusal visibility, material consequence disclosure, current decision state, and system-applied pressure must be evaluated.

visual_findings.source_observation: The deck argues that presentation/distribution can materially change outcomes even when the underlying product is similar.
The deck recommends concentrating effort on a small number of high-leverage factors instead of optimizing everything equally.
visual_findings.attack_translation: Pareto/leverage claims may prioritize work but may not skip unique safety, evidence, or authority obligations.

visual_findings.source_observation: The deck explicitly proposes changing the market/reference frame to change perceived price/value comparisons.
visual_findings.attack_translation: Changing the comparator can change an apparent result without changing the system. Before/after claims therefore remain bound to a frozen reference class and measurement protocol.

visual_findings.source_observation: The deck explicitly sells the backend only after multiple screening/education steps and describes the remaining audience as higher-intent or better-fit customers.
visual_findings.attack_translation: Evidence measured after a deliberate selection funnel is evidence about that selected cohort. It cannot silently become evidence about the original population.

visual_findings.source_observation: The deck repeatedly uses education, free value, CTA exposure, payment, fan formation, and prior purchase to change later willingness, expectations, and repeat behavior.
visual_findings.attack_translation: Later observations are conditional on the path of prior interventions; post-intervention state is not automatically an intrinsic baseline property.

visual_findings.source_observation: Repeated middle-tier purchases are described as capable of increasing expectations for later offers and changing downstream economics.
visual_findings.attack_translation: A locally successful repeated intervention can mutate downstream expectations and therefore must be evaluated against the protected end-to-end outcome.

visual_findings.source_observation: The summary shows content selection via Reduce/Reuse/Recycle and a PASTOR-like script sequence.
visual_findings.attack_translation: Useful as content-production adapters, not universal Ultimate Loop doctrine.
